scenario_text: An enzyme converts a single soluble substrate while enzyme concentration, temperature, and pH are fixed. Initial product-formation rate is measured immediately after mixing across independently prepared substrate concentrations. Binding-site occupancy limits how much enzyme-substrate complex can form, so the response approaches a finite catalytic ceiling. Product buildup, substrate inhibition, and enzyme deactivation are negligible during the measurement.

spec.target_description: Initial product-formation rate in micromolar product per second.
expected_behaviors: The rate is zero when substrate is absent.
The rate increases approximately linearly at very low substrate concentration.
The response remains nonnegative and approaches a finite plateau with diminishing slope.
forbidden_behaviors: A decline in rate at high substrate concentration.
A cooperative threshold or sigmoidal transition.
Negative rates or unbounded growth with substrate concentration.

scenario_text: A soluble enzyme is catalytically competent only after two identical monomers assemble into a homodimer, and substrate is held saturating. Separate assays vary total enzyme concentration within a dilute regime where only a small fraction of the monomers dimerize. Rapid monomer-dimer equilibration makes active-dimer abundance rise approximately with the second power of total enzyme concentration. Initial product formation is measured before aggregation or enzyme loss can occur.

spec.target_description: Initial catalytic rate generated by the active enzyme dimer.

input_symbols.description: Total monomer-equivalent enzyme concentration in micromolar.

expected_behaviors: The rate vanishes when no enzyme is present.
The response is strongly convex over the specified dilute range.
Doubling total enzyme produces approximately a fourfold rate increase away from the zero boundary.
forbidden_behaviors: A nonzero intercept at zero enzyme concentration.
A purely linear enzyme-dose response.
A concave saturation plateau within the stipulated dilute range.

scenario_text: A hydrolase is productive when one substrate molecule occupies its catalytic site. At high substrate concentration, a second substrate molecule binds the enzyme-substrate complex and traps it in a nonproductive state. Initial rates are measured over a concentration range spanning both productive occupancy and formation of the trapped complex. The intended response therefore rises to one maximum and then loses activity as excess substrate accumulates.

spec.target_description: Initial hydrolysis rate in micromolar product per second.
expected_behaviors: The rate is zero without substrate.
The response has one interior maximum.
Activity declines smoothly at high substrate concentration while remaining nonnegative.
forbidden_behaviors: A monotonic approach to a nonzero high-substrate plateau.
Negative catalytic rates.
Multiple peaks, oscillations, or discontinuities.

scenario_text: Two active-site residues control catalysis: one must be protonated and the other must be deprotonated. Turnover frequency is measured at saturating substrate across independently buffered pH values, with temperature and ionic strength fixed. Activity is low when either required protonation state is rare and highest within an intermediate pH window. Binding saturation and enzyme denaturation are excluded so that active-site acid-base speciation is the sole source of curvature.

spec.target_description: Catalytic turnover frequency per second at saturating substrate.
expected_behaviors: The response is smooth and nonnegative.
Turnover has one maximum at an intermediate pH.
Activity is suppressed toward both acidic and basic limits, with possible asymmetry between the two sides.
forbidden_behaviors: A monotonic response across the full pH range.
A high-activity plateau at both pH extremes.
Discontinuities, negative turnover, or repeated peaks.

scenario_text: A purified enzyme reversibly interconverts two substrates, A and B, with two products, P and Q. The signed initial net flux is measured while all four solute concentrations are independently varied and the enzyme amount is fixed. Forward and reverse catalytic cycles compete for the same finite enzyme pool, allowing the flux to pass continuously through zero and change direction. Cofactors, pH, and temperature remain fixed throughout the assays.

spec.target_description: Signed initial net catalytic flux, positive in the direction of product formation.

input_symbols.description: Concentration of the first forward substrate in millimolar.
Concentration of the second forward substrate in millimolar.
Concentration of the first product and reverse substrate in millimolar.
Concentration of the second product and reverse substrate in millimolar.

expected_behaviors: Forward substrates favor positive flux, whereas accumulated products favor negative flux.
The net rate changes sign continuously across a composition-dependent balance surface.
With products absent, forward turnover vanishes if either required forward substrate is absent.
Flux magnitude is limited by the finite enzyme pool at high solute concentrations.
forbidden_behaviors: A rate that is always nonnegative regardless of product concentrations.
Unbounded flux growth at high concentrations.
Discontinuities or singularities within the sampled concentration range.
Forward turnover with products absent when one required forward substrate is missing.

scenario_text: An enzyme is assayed with saturating substrate over a narrow temperature interval in which it remains fully folded. The chemistry-limited turnover step crosses a fixed activation barrier, while binding and product release are much faster. Independent samples at each temperature report the instantaneous rate constant of that chemical step. Thermal deactivation, solvent transitions, and viscosity changes are excluded from the experiment.

spec.target_description: Rate constant per second for the enzyme-catalyzed chemical conversion step.
expected_behaviors: The rate constant remains strictly positive.
The response increases smoothly and with upward curvature over the specified interval.
Equal temperature increments produce approximately multiplicative changes in rate.
forbidden_behaviors: A temperature-induced activity maximum or downturn.
A finite saturation plateau within the specified interval.
Negative, discontinuous, or oscillatory rate constants.

scenario_text: A nonreactive substrate analog is rapidly mixed with an enzyme that closes only after initial encounter binding. The assay tracks free enzyme E, free ligand L, encounter complex C, and closed complex D over the first 30 seconds. Association creates C, which can either dissociate or reversibly isomerize into D. The benchmark targets transient encounter-complex kinetics rather than an equilibrium binding curve.

spec.target_description: Time derivative of the encounter-complex concentration.

required_dynamic_states.description: Closed ligand-bound complex concentration in micromolar.

expected_behaviors: Encounter-complex formation initially responds to both free enzyme and free ligand availability.
C can exhibit a transient peak as closed complex D accumulates.
The total amount of enzyme and the total amount of ligand are each conserved.
All states relax toward a nonnegative stationary binding distribution.
forbidden_behaviors: Instantaneous elimination of the encounter complex.
Negative concentrations or loss of enzyme material.
Persistent oscillations in the closed binding system.
Independent evolution of bound states that violates ligand conservation.

scenario_text: A small seed of active protease is mixed with its inactive zymogen precursor. Each active molecule cleaves an inactive precursor molecule, creating another active molecule with the same specificity. Total protease-related material is normalized and conserved, so only the active fraction a must be evolved and the inactive fraction is its complement. Spontaneous activation and active-protease loss are absent during the five-minute record.

spec.target_description: Time derivative of the dimensionless active-protease fraction.

required_dynamic_states.description: Fraction of the conserved protease pool in the active form.

expected_behaviors: The active fraction increases monotonically from a nonzero seed.
Activation accelerates while active protease and precursor are both abundant, then slows as precursor is exhausted.
The active fraction remains bounded between zero and one.
An exactly zero active seed would remain inactive in the absence of spontaneous activation.
forbidden_behaviors: Overshoot beyond the conserved active fraction.
Unbounded exponential growth.
A decline in active fraction without an inactivation pathway.
Activation from an exactly zero seed.

scenario_text: A cofactor-buffered enzyme network cycles three small metabolites S, X, and I. A fixed pool of the first enzyme converts S to X, a slower second enzyme converts X to I, and a third enzyme recycles I to S. I also binds allosterically to the first enzyme and suppresses its catalytic activity, creating delayed negative feedback. Enzyme amounts and kinetic constants are fixed in a regime that supports sustained concentration oscillations.

spec.target_description: Time derivative of intermediate X concentration.

required_dynamic_states.description: Concentration of the substrate metabolite in millimolar.
Concentration of the catalytic intermediate in millimolar.
Concentration of the recycled allosteric inhibitor in millimolar.

expected_behaviors: After a transient, all three metabolites exhibit bounded sustained oscillations.
X and I show a reproducible phase lag caused by the slower inhibitor-producing step.
The derivative of X alternates sign during each cycle.
Total material across the three metabolite forms remains conserved and all concentrations remain nonnegative.
forbidden_behaviors: Monotonic convergence to a fixed concentration in the stipulated oscillatory regime.
Unbounded amplitude growth or long-term concentration drift.
Negative metabolite concentrations.
Oscillations that violate conservation of the cycled metabolite pool.

scenario_text: An enzyme assay runs with buffered substrate, active enzyme E, and accumulated product P. At 40 seconds, a large prescribed bolus of covalent inhibitor is added; before that intervention its concentration is negligible, and afterward it remains constant in excess. Active enzyme is irreversibly converted into covalent adduct EI, while only unmodified E can produce P. The inhibitor protocol is prescribed background rather than an additional dynamic state.

spec.target_description: Time derivative of product concentration during the inhibitor-pulse assay.

required_dynamic_states.description: Covalent enzyme-inhibitor adduct concentration in micromolar.

expected_behaviors: Before 40 seconds, active enzyme is nearly constant and product accumulates at a nearly constant rate.
State concentrations remain continuous at the intervention time while their derivatives enter a new regime.
After inhibitor addition, E decreases monotonically, EI increases, and product formation progressively slows.
Total enzyme material across E and EI remains conserved.
forbidden_behaviors: An inhibitor effect before the prescribed pulse.
Instantaneous jumps in E, EI, or P at the intervention time.
Recovery of active enzyme from the irreversible adduct.
A decrease in accumulated product or a negative product-formation rate.

scenario_text: A closed population occupies a habitat with fixed resource supply and no seasonal forcing. Births exceed deaths at low abundance, while crowding progressively lowers net recruitment near a habitat-supported ceiling. Replicate trajectories begin both below and above that ceiling and are followed for many generations. The regression target is the instantaneous change in total population abundance.

spec.target_description: Instantaneous net rate of change of total population abundance.

required_dynamic_states.description: Total number of individuals in the closed habitat.

expected_behaviors: Growth is nearly proportional to abundance at low positive density.
The rate of change is positive below the habitat-supported ceiling and negative above it.
Zero abundance and one positive ceiling abundance have zero net change.
Positive trajectories approach the ceiling monotonically from either side.
forbidden_behaviors: A low-density threshold below which all positive populations decline.
Positive growth above the habitat-supported ceiling.
Persistent oscillations under constant conditions.
Negative abundance or finite-time divergence.

scenario_text: An obligately outcrossing population lives in a fixed habitat where successful reproduction requires encounters between potential mates. Sparse populations experience too few encounters to replace mortality, so abundance declines below a critical level. At intermediate abundance recruitment exceeds mortality, whereas crowding causes decline again at high abundance. Populations are initialized on both sides of the low-density threshold, and the target is their instantaneous rate of change.

spec.target_description: Instantaneous net population change under mate limitation and high-density crowding.

required_dynamic_states.description: Abundance of the obligately outcrossing population.

expected_behaviors: Zero abundance has zero net change.
Small positive populations decline toward extinction.
Growth becomes positive above a low unstable threshold and remains positive until a higher balance point.
Abundance above the high balance point declines toward it.
forbidden_behaviors: Positive growth at every sufficiently small positive abundance.
Only one positive balance abundance.
Unbounded high-density growth.
Self-sustained oscillations under fixed conditions.

scenario_text: Short feeding trials measure prey removal by individual predators under constant environmental conditions. Prey density is independently set before each trial, and trials are brief enough that depletion does not appreciably alter that density. Search limits consumption when prey are scarce, while handling each captured prey imposes a finite upper feeding rate at high density. The target is prey consumed per predator per unit time.

spec.target_description: Per-predator prey consumption rate during a short feeding trial.

input_symbols.description: Experimentally set prey density in individuals per hectare.

expected_behaviors: Consumption is zero when prey are absent.
Consumption is approximately proportional to prey density when prey are scarce.
Additional prey produce progressively smaller increases in consumption.
Consumption approaches a finite positive upper rate at high prey density.
forbidden_behaviors: Unbounded linear growth at high prey density.
Declining consumption as prey become abundant.
A low-density reproductive threshold or delayed population feedback.
Negative consumption rates.

scenario_text: Two species share a fixed habitat and compete for the same limiting opportunities. Each species suppresses its own recruitment through crowding and also reduces the other species' recruitment as competitor abundance rises. Interaction strengths are fixed so that within-species limitation is stronger than cross-species limitation, allowing stable coexistence from positive initial abundances. The target is the instantaneous change in species 1, with both species evolved jointly.

spec.target_description: Instantaneous net rate of change of species 1 abundance under reciprocal competition.
expected_behaviors: Species 1 has zero net change from demographic processes when it is absent.
At fixed positive species 1 abundance, increasing species 2 abundance lowers species 1 growth.
Strong own-species or competitor crowding makes species 1 decline.
Positive trajectories of both species approach a stable coexistence state.
forbidden_behaviors: A positive effect of either competitor on the other's growth.
Predator-prey sign structure between the two species.
Persistent cycles under fixed interaction strengths.
Dependence on an unlisted dynamic resource state.

scenario_text: A population is divided into juvenile and reproductive adult classes. Adults add offspring only to the juvenile class, juveniles mature into adults, and each class has a fixed per-capita mortality rate. Rates are constant, with no crowding or seasonal forcing, and are chosen so the two classes approach a stable composition while total abundance grows. The target is the instantaneous change in adult abundance, so both classes must be evolved jointly from their initial values.

spec.target_description: Instantaneous net rate of change of reproductive adult abundance.
expected_behaviors: Adult change increases with juvenile abundance through maturation.
Adult change decreases with adult abundance through adult mortality.
Juvenile maturation appears as an adult gain and a corresponding juvenile loss.
After a transient, both classes share a common exponential trend and a stable abundance ratio.
forbidden_behaviors: Direct addition of newborns to the adult class.
Density-dependent ceilings or low-density thresholds.
Independent adult dynamics that omit juvenile abundance.
Seasonal or self-sustained oscillations.

scenario_text: Destination habitat patches receive immigrants from otherwise identical source patches across a homogeneous intervening landscape. Only source-to-destination separation is varied independently, while source abundance, departure rate, and landscape quality remain fixed. Each additional unit of travel distance removes the same proportion of the dispersers still in transit. The target is the successful immigrant arrival rate per source individual.

spec.target_description: Successful immigrant arrival rate per source individual at a destination patch.

input_symbols.description: Distance between source and destination habitat patches in kilometers.

expected_behaviors: Arrival rate is maximal at zero separation.
Equal increments of distance reduce the remaining arrival rate by the same proportion.
Arrival declines smoothly and remains positive over finite distances.
Arrival approaches zero at very large separation.
forbidden_behaviors: A hard dispersal cutoff within the sampled distance range.
Increasing or nonmonotonic arrival with distance.
A heavy tail with no characteristic decay distance.
Negative arrival rates.

scenario_text: A single population is followed for eight years in a habitat where reproductive conditions repeat annually. Per-capita recruitment varies smoothly with calendar phase, while mortality and crowding coefficients remain fixed. The recurring favorable and unfavorable seasons drive a bounded, phase-locked cycle rather than an autonomous approach to constant abundance. The target is instantaneous population change as a function of the evolving abundance and explicit time.

spec.target_description: Instantaneous population change under smooth annual variation in recruitment.

required_dynamic_states.description: Population abundance exposed to annual recruitment seasonality.

expected_behaviors: At a fixed abundance, the rate of change repeats after each annual period.
Growth is favored during one recurring part of the year and suppressed during another.
After transients, abundance approaches a bounded cycle with fixed calendar phase.
A population beginning nonnegative remains nonnegative.
forbidden_behaviors: An autonomous rate depending only on abundance.
A drifting or changing seasonal period.
Abrupt seasonal jumps when forcing is specified as smooth.
An additional dynamic environmental state.

scenario_text: A large network contains many identical habitat patches that can be occupied or empty. Occupied patches seed vacant patches, while local extinction empties occupied patches at a fixed per-patch rate. Colonization and extinction rates are independently set across landscapes, and a small nonzero seed of occupancy is assumed whenever colonization can persist. The target is the attracting equilibrium fraction occupied, which is zero below a colonization threshold and positive above it.

spec.target_description: Attracting long-run fraction of habitat patches occupied.

input_symbols.description: Per-year colonization rate among habitat patches.
Per-year local extinction rate of occupied patches.

expected_behaviors: The selected equilibrium is all-empty when colonization cannot outpace extinction.
Occupancy rises continuously from zero after colonization exceeds the threshold.
At fixed extinction, occupancy increases with colonization and approaches full occupancy.
At fixed colonization, occupancy decreases as local extinction increases.
forbidden_behaviors: Positive equilibrium occupancy below the persistence threshold.
Negative occupancy or occupancy greater than one.
Increasing occupancy with greater extinction rate.
Dependence on the precise positive seed occupancy.

scenario_text: On a large stationary landscape, circular neighborhoods are centered on randomly chosen focal individuals and additional conspecifics are counted. Habitat quality and regional abundance are fixed, but the aggregation pattern has no characteristic scale over the surveyed distances. Neighborhood radius is independently varied, and circles affected by landscape edges are excluded. The target is the mean cumulative number of additional conspecifics around a focal individual.

spec.target_description: Mean cumulative number of additional conspecifics within a neighborhood of radius R.

input_symbols.description: Radius of the circular neighborhood in meters.

expected_behaviors: Expected neighbor count increases monotonically with neighborhood radius.
The relationship is approximately straight when both radius and count are viewed on logarithmic scales.
A fixed multiplicative increase in radius produces a consistent multiplicative increase in expected count.
No plateau or characteristic spatial scale appears within the sampled range.
forbidden_behaviors: A finite-radius saturation plateau within the sampled range.
A characteristic exponential cutoff in cumulative count.
An additive focal-individual offset, because the focal individual is excluded.
Temporal population growth or decline as part of the response.

scenario_text: A closed harvested population has low-density recruitment proportional to abundance, while crowding suppresses natural production at high abundance. Managers remove a fixed quota per unit time whenever individuals remain, and removal stops once the population reaches extinction. The quota is below maximum natural production, creating a low abundance threshold that separates collapse from recovery toward a higher balance. The target is the instantaneous net change in abundance across trajectories starting on both sides of that threshold.

spec.target_description: Instantaneous net change in harvested population abundance under a fixed removal quota.

required_dynamic_states.description: Abundance of the closed population subject to fixed-quota removal.

expected_behaviors: Net change is negative at low positive abundance, positive at intermediate abundance, and negative again at high abundance.
There are two positive balance abundances, with the lower one unstable and the upper one stable.
Trajectories starting below the lower threshold reach extinction, while those above it approach the upper balance.
Extinction is absorbing because removal stops when no individuals remain.
forbidden_behaviors: Continuation to negative population abundance.
Harvest loss that vanishes in direct proportion to abundance.
Only one positive balance abundance under the specified subcritical quota.
Seasonal or self-sustained population cycles.
